["Real Hope, Real Change — for a fairer, greener Britain. I strongly support a bold, joined-up plan that puts people and planet first. We must accelerate the roll-out of renewable energy — more offshore and onshore wind, community solar and locally owned projects — so cheap, clean power is available to every town and village. To cut emissions and household costs, I strongly support banning the sale of new petrol cars by 2030 and ensuring every new home is built with non-fossil-fuel heating, rooftop solar and high levels of insulation. Warm homes and affordable electric travel will save money and create skilled local jobs.

I also strongly support a carbon tax on fossil fuel sales, with revenues returned to the public as a dividend — making the transition fairer, not regressive. And because climate breakdown is global, I strongly support compensating people in other countries who are already suffering its effects.

This is about justice: public ownership of our energy, investing in communities, and sharing the benefits broadly. For the common good — fairer, greener communities and a secure future for everyone."]
text:
Accelerate the roll-out of renewable energy production (more offshore and onshore wind parks)
- Slightly support. I want to move away from fossil fuels and make clean power widely available, and I like the emphasis on community and locally owned projects. But I’m cautious about large-scale infrastructure that can harm landscapes and ecosystems or be imposed top-down without meaningful local consent.

Ban new oil/gas/coal licences
- Slightly support. I think we shouldn’t keep opening the door for fossil fuel extraction, and new licences send the wrong signal. At the same time I worry about energy security, jobs, and transitional impacts on communities that depend on these industries, so I’d want the ban paired with clear plans for a just transition.

Ban the sale of new petrol cars by no later than 2030
- Slightly support. The goal of rapid electrification makes sense for emissions reductions and aligns with wanting cleaner transport, but a 2030 deadline feels fast and could hit lower-income households hardest unless there’s strong support (subsidies, affordable used EV markets, better public transport). I support it if the policy is accompanied by equitable measures.

Mandate that all new housing developments have non-fossil heating, rooftop solar and high levels of insulation
- Slightly support. Building low-carbon homes from the start is sensible and cost-effective long-term, and it fits with future-proofing homes. My concern is that strict mandates could raise upfront costs and worsen affordability unless there are measures to keep housing accessible.

Impose a carbon tax on fossil fuel sales and distribute revenues to the public (carbon fee and dividend)
- Neutral / middle. I see the fairness appeal of returning revenues to people and the incentive effects of pricing carbon, but I’m unsure market-based mechanisms are enough to drive deep systemic change. I’m also worried about short-term cost impacts on lower-income households even with dividends — the design details matter a great deal.

Compensate people in other countries who are impacted by climate change
- Slightly support. I agree there’s a justice argument for compensation — countries and communities suffering most deserve support. Yet I’m uncertain about the effectiveness of international transfers and whether funds reach the people who need them; I’d want robust, accountable delivery mechanisms.

Reflection (thinking out loud)
Overall the package appeals to my values: it prioritises people and the planet and pushes for public benefit rather than letting fossil fuel interests keep profiting. The parts I find most convincing are community-led renewables and the focus on making homes energy-efficient — these seem tangible and locally beneficial. I’m more hesitant about blanket bans and market tools (like a carbon fee) without clear, equitable transition measures for workers and lower-income households. International compensation is principled but raises practical questions about implementation and accountability. My support tends to be conditional: I favour ambitious action, but only if paired with well-designed, equitable safeguards and meaningful local involvement.

Ban new oil/gas/coal licences: Slightly oppose.
